examples.solution_text:
Use EST $2$ at the starting vertex, LST $11$ at the ending vertex and duration $4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}11-4-2\\&=5\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$
Activity $A$ is non-critical. It can be delayed by up to $5$ hours from its earliest start without delaying project completion.

(a) For each edge, subtract its duration and starting EST from its ending LST. Use duration $0$ for the dummy.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Float of }A&=6-6-0=0\\\text{Float of }B&=7-4-0=3\\\text{Float of }C&=8-2-6=0\\\text{Float of }D&=10-3-4=3\\\text{Float of }E&=12-4-8=0\\\text{Float of }F&=12-2-8=2\\\text{Float of }G&=15-3-12=0\\\text{Float of dummy}&=10-0-8=2\end{aligned}$
All float times are in days.
(b) Zero float identifies a critical activity. The four critical activities are $A$, $C$, $E$ and $G$. The dummy is non-critical despite having duration $0$.
(c) Activities $B$ and $D$ each have a float of $3$ days. Comparing all float times, these two activities share the longest float.
